divergences.owner: the Go prompt slice (https://github.com/jeiang/atrium/issues/125) decides how to handle the text; until it does, a Go body may differ from these goldens at system[0].text only by the run_code sentence
divergences.what: tells the model to call run_code for several read-only lookups; run_code is not ported in Phase A and is absent from every tools list here
names run_code as a separate interpreter; the code sandbox and run_code are both not ported in Phase A
divergences.where: files.SANDBOX_PROMPT (sent only with the thread code sandbox on, so in no golden here)

paths: code_execution tool and container (thread code sandbox)
excluded.reason: not ported in Phase A (https://github.com/jeiang/atrium/issues/19, https://github.com/jeiang/atrium/issues/96 review fixes S7)

scenarios.description: Chat run at the default effort and 5m TTL: tool_use (profile_get) then end_turn. System = SYSTEM + profile + skills index; breakpoints on SYSTEM, the last stable block, the last tool and the last user block.
scenarios.name: chat_tool_turn

scenarios.description: Two chat runs in one thread: each operator message keeps the date stamp of its own run and the history breakpoint moves to the newest user block.
scenarios.name: chat_followup_turn

scenarios.description: cache_ttl_chat = 1h: the chat run's prefix and history breakpoints carry ttl 1h (bug #67); a cron run in the same instance keeps the 5m default.
scenarios.name: cache_ttl_1h

scenarios.description: A response stopped with pause_turn (server tool still running) is journaled and the loop sends the continuation request unchanged in shape.
scenarios.name: pause_turn

scenarios.description: web_search_20260318 declared last with allowed_callers [direct] (bug #68); the server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result blocks return unchanged in the next turn.
scenarios.name: web_search

scenarios.description: Server-side compaction (compact_20260112, pause_after_compaction): the compaction block opens the next request, followed by the context manifest and the operator's message with its stamp; thinking is stripped.
scenarios.name: server_compaction

scenarios.description: A compaction response whose usage.iterations bills every iteration (bug #65); the usage rows hold the summed tokens and the >100K tier.
scenarios.name: usage_iterations

scenarios.description: Preflight over 95% of the 90K limit compacts on the client: one tool-free, thinking-free create() at effort low with the summary system prompt, then the run resumes from summary + manifest + the operator's message.
scenarios.name: client_compaction

scenarios.description: A thread at effort high and the 1M context limit: clear_tool_uses and compact triggers scale with the limit; a response reporting an applied clear_tool_uses edit is metered.
scenarios.name: context_limit_1m_clear_edits

scenarios.description: output_config.effort = low; max_tokens follows the effort (16384).
scenarios.name: effort_low

scenarios.description: output_config.effort = xhigh; max_tokens follows the effort (65536).
scenarios.name: effort_xhigh

scenarios.description: output_config.effort = max; max_tokens follows the effort (65536).
scenarios.name: effort_max

scenarios.description: A chat run calls research(role=web): the child sub run sends its own request (allowlisted tools + web_search, digest rules and the agent prompt as the last cached system block), then the parent continues with the digest.
scenarios.name: subagent_research

scenarios.description: A thread in a project: the project block (instructions + wiki hub) follows the cached prefix uncached; effort and context limit come from the project.
scenarios.name: project_thread

scenarios.description: Chat attachments without the code sandbox: PDF as a base64 document, PNG as a base64 image, Markdown, .docx and .xlsx as extracted-text documents (title, untrusted context, citations), ahead of the operator text; a second turn rebuilds them from storage.
scenarios.name: chat_attachments

scenarios.description: A project file joins the first user turn of every request in the project's threads, ahead of a 'Project files' note and the operator text.
scenarios.name: project_files

scenarios.description: A scheduled job run by the scheduler: kind cron, effort high, operator-written prompt, 5m TTL, web_search offered.
scenarios.name: cron_run

scenarios.description: The seeded nightly job: kind nightly, effort high, NIGHTLY_PROMPT with the wiki-capture skill expanded, nightly tool set, no web_search.
scenarios.name: nightly_run
